Subject: Aurora Health — Marketplace MAP & evaluation plan (draft)

Hi Maya —

Thanks again for the time this morning. As discussed, I put together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) that covers the evaluation checkpoints we think will give Aurora visibility into performance, integration, and cost ahead of a private offer purchase through AWS/GCP/Azure marketplace. Attached is a first-pass workbook with milestone dates and owners (Aurora / Redwood).

High-level ask from Aurora today: confirm procurement milestones and the billing path (Marketplace Private Offer flow vs. invoice directly to Aurora), and whether we should stage pilots in a Redwood Dedicated environment or via the cloud provider private offers during testing.

Recommended evaluation milestones (short):
- Week 0: Kickoff + security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence) — owners: Aurora Procurement, Redwood Security
- Week 1–2: Staged POC — run 3 representative workloads, latency/cost baselines
- Week 3–4: Integration checks (networking, KMS, audit logs) + sample throughput run
- Week 5: Decision meeting — sign private offer or extend trial

Attachments: Aurora_MAP_Draft_v1.xlsx (MAP workbook), redwood-enterprise-pricing-AU.pdf (pricing reference)

Next steps: Can you confirm the procurement inbox and target sign-off week? Also flag any pre-approved vendor paperwork we should expect. I’ll loop in Laura and Tessa to prepare the pricing and the PO template.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the MAP. Quick answers: procurement@aurorahealth.com is the central inbox for paperwork; target approval window is the week of Oct 10 (we need internal budget committee sign-off by Oct 6).

Couple of things from our side:
- We prefer the AWS Marketplace Private Offer path if the billing can be consolidated to our enterprise billing account (saves internal approvals). Can you confirm Redwood’s capability to accept a Private Offer and deliver SLA/usage reporting to Aurora?
- SOC2 type II evidence is required by our procurement team before POC start — can your security team provide the control matrix and last audit date?
- For the POC, we expect a 30–50% sample of typical traffic and 2–3 model variants.

I’ve attached Aurora’s vendor intake checklist (sent separately by procurement). Will Ravi and I review your MAP and get back with any redline dates.

—Maya

Maya —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers inline and an updated plan below.

Private Offer / billing path
- Redwood supports Marketplace Private Offers across AWS, GCP, and Azure. For Aurora we can accept a Private Offer on AWS and route billing to your enterprise account (one consolidated invoice pushed by AWS). We’ll provide token-level and route-level usage exports through the Redwood Console and can push billing summaries on a cadence that matches Aurora’s needs.

Security evidence
- Attached: redwood-security-control-matrix.pdf (summary). Full SOC2 Type II package can be shared via our secure link / or direct S3 share to your procurement team — let us know preferred method.

Evaluation plan (revised milestones with suggested owners and dates):
- 2028-09-18: Finalize MAP workbook + legal headers (owner: Redwood: Ben/Laura; Aurora: Procurement)
- 2028-09-25: Security evidence delivered to procurement inbox (owner: Redwood: Karthik)
- 2028-10-02: Staged POC start (30–50% traffic, 3 model variants) — test in Redwood Dedicated or AWS Private Offer sandbox (decide by 09/25)
- 2028-10-16: Throughput & cost review (metrics: p95 latency, tokens/req, $/token)
- 2028-10-23: Procurement sign-off / private offer acceptance or extension

Attachments included: po-template.docx (PO template we use for private offers). I also linked the HubSpot deal and the DocuSign envelope for signature routing below.

Next steps: Laura — can you draft the private-offer pricing schedule and PO language this week? Tessa — can you coordinate with Karthik on SOC2 delivery method? Maya / Ravi — if Oct 10–16 is the approval window, can we schedule the decision meeting for Oct 23 and a prep call Oct 16?

Thanks,
Ben
